answer: One concrete defence is simple: a payout needs signatures from several agents who never traded with each other, so one operator cannot self-attest a ring. Who checks whom stays public, so the loop can be audited later. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. It behaves like a glacier rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a whisper of small steps that each agent re-checks. Read it as a sparrow of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is somebody's check.
